reason: The text explicitly depicts multiple non-leaders exercising significant agency. The men of Shechem (common people) collectively choose to make Abimelech king. The hired rêqîm (worthless men) execute violence against Jotham's brothers. Gaal son of Ebed, a non-leader, persuades the people to rebel, and they trust in him and follow him. The people of Shechem initially support Abimelech through their own choice, then later turn against him at Gaal's urging. Most strikingly, an unnamed woman at the tower of Thebez independently acts to kill Abimelech by dropping a millstone on his head—a non-leader taking decisive action that determines the outcome. The narrative demonstrates that ordinary people and even individuals of low status exercise meaningful agency in shaping events.
